hero.h1: Learn to work with the life in your soil
hero.intro: Whether you’re growing in your backyard raised beds or advising thousand-acre farms, there’s a path for you. Choose from self-paced or group classes, online or in person. Every program is grounded in decades of research and practice and designed to deliver practical skills and insights.

elaine.line: Dr. Elaine said she could train anyone to use a microscope in one day. Our programs start there: you learn to see the bacteria, fungi, protozoa and nematodes in your own soil and compost, and what each one tells you.

source.credit: Dr. Elaine Ingham, “How to Build Great Soil, Part 1”, Diego Footer, 28:52

pathSelector.h2: What brings you to the soil food web?
pathSelector._note: Each chip jumps to the program that serves that person. 'I grow food' lands on the Foundation Courses, the starting point for everyone, until Decision 1 settles what a grower who does not want the Consultant title buys instead.

programs.name: Foundation Courses
programs.tagline: The complete introduction to the soil food web
programs.body: Understand soil from new dimensions, meet the soil food web organisms and understand their ecosystem role, and learn the fundamentals of farming microbes in compost and applying them with compost extracts and teas. The prerequisites for our Advanced Programs.

cta.label: See the Foundation Courses on the school site

programs.name: Advanced Programs
programs.tagline: Soil Microscopy · BioComplete™ Compost Production · Biological Liquid Amendments · Field Trials
programs.body: Complete all four, the Complete Practicum, to earn the Soil Food Web Consultant title and join our professional directory. Complete the Soil Microscopy program to earn the Soil Food Web Lab-Tech title.

cta.label: See the Complete Practicum on the school site

soilMicroscopyElaine.line: Learn to read a drop of soil the way Dr. Elaine did. Count fungal hyphae, spot flagellates and ciliates, and tell when compost is tipping anaerobic before it harms roots.

items.q: Do I need a science background?
items.a: No. The courses are designed for people with no relevant experience. The Foundation Courses build everything from first principles, at your pace.

items.q: How long do the programs take?
items.note: VERIFY typical completion ranges per program with the education team.

items.a: The Foundation Courses need only a computer and curiosity. The Microscopy program requires a microscope. Guidance on affordable models is provided inside the course.

items.q: What do the professional titles mean?
items.a: Soil Food Web Consultant: completed the full Complete Practicum (all four Advanced Programs). Soil Food Web Lab-Tech: completed the Microscopy Advanced Program. Both titles are earned, and both appear in our professionals directory.

items.q: What if it’s not for me?
items.a: Every course carries a 30-day, no-questions-asked money-back guarantee, provided you’ve watched no more than one-third of the lectures.

items.q: I can’t afford the courses. Are there options?
items.a: Yes. Our scholarship program is growing, with priority for applicants in under-resourced regions. See the Scholarships page.
